docdesigner User Manual

Source: USER-MANUAL.md

docdesigner has two outputs:

  • docdesigner::pdf creates a designed PDF document.
  • docdesigner::html creates plain body HTML for WordPress or another CMS.

The main design principle is simple YAML. A field should appear in YAML only when it changes the document, identifies the document, or helps publishing.

Start a Document

Create a starter:

docdesigner::designer_use(template = "pdf")
docdesigner::designer_use(template = "html")

Or use RStudio:

File > New File > R Markdown > From Template

Updating Templates

Most projects should use bundled package assets. In that workflow, the update path is simply:

# reinstall or update docdesigner

After the package is updated, documents using docdesigner::pdf or docdesigner::html use the updated bundled assets automatically.

If a project keeps editable local copies, refresh those copies from the installed package:

docdesigner::designer_update_templates()

To pull the latest assets from GitHub instead:

docdesigner::designer_update_templates(source = "github", branch = "main")

That updates:

  • docdesignertemplate.tex
  • default.csl
  • fonts/
  • sets/

Minimal YAML

PDF:

---
title: "Document Title"
author: "Your Name"
output:
  docdesigner::pdf:
    style: policy
---

PDF options:

---
title: "Document Title"
author:
  - name: "First Author"
    dept: "Department of Sociology"
    inst: "Queens College, CUNY"
    address: "65-30 Kissena Blvd, Queens, NY 11367"
    email: "first.author@example.edu"
    web: "example.edu/~first"
  - name: "Second Author"
warning: "DRAFT IN PROGRESS: DO NOT CIRCULATE"
acknowledgements: |
  I thank the department's workshop for comments.
output:
  docdesigner::pdf:
    style: methods
    title_layout: page
    doublespace: true
---
  • doublespace: true double-spaces the body text, as for a manuscript under review. Titles, headings, tables, captions, footnotes and code stay single-spaced.
  • title_layout: page gives the title, byline and abstract a page of their own; header (the default in every style) sets them at the top of page 1.
  • author is a plain string or a list of people. Each person’s name appears in the byline, with several authors stacked. The corresponding author (marked corresponding: true, otherwise the first author with an address, email or web) gets a contact block: name, dept and inst, address, and linked email and web. orcid is accepted but not printed yet.
  • kicker replaces the small label some styles set above the title (“POLICY BRIEF” in policy, “WORKING PAPER” in ssrn and economist): kicker: "Research Brief". kicker: "" removes it, and any style accepts one.
  • warning is a line such as “DRAFT IN PROGRESS: DO NOT CIRCULATE”, set between two rules. acknowledgements (or acknowledgments) is a paragraph or more of thanks.
  • On a title page the contact block, the warning and the acknowledgements stack at the foot of the page, in that order. In the header layout the warning sits above the title, and the contact details and acknowledgements become an unnumbered note at the foot of page 1.

Warning: tables in two-column styles (nature, economist). A two-column page cannot hold a table that breaks across pages, so in these styles every table becomes a float, placed by LaTeX:

  • A table may not appear where you put it. It moves to the top of a column or page, often after the paragraph that follows it. Refer to tables by number (“Table 2”), never as “the table below”.
  • A table that fits one column stays in the column; a wider one spans both columns and moves to the top of the next page that has room.
  • A table is never split. One taller than a page runs off the bottom. Keep tables short, or split them yourself.
  • Column widths are not kept. Text in cells does not wrap, so a long cell widens the whole table. Keep cell text short.

For long or wide tables, use a single-column style.

HTML:

---
title: "Article Title"
author: "Your Name"
output:
  docdesigner::html
---

Style Gallery

Styles apply to docdesigner::pdf. They do not apply to docdesigner::html.

Sixteen styles ship in two sets: academic (minimal, modern, nature, methods, demography, ssrn, sociology, ajs, thesis, qc-thesis) and public (policy, government, economist, atlantic, humanities, bulletin).

Writing a thesis

Two styles set a thesis: thesis, plain and conservative, and qc-thesis, the same with the Queens College title page for the MA in Data Analytics and Applied Social Research. Both use the thesis title layout: a title page with the degree statement, an optional copyright page, then contents, acknowledgements and abstract numbered i, ii, iii, with chapters starting on new pages from page 1.

---
title: "Thesis Title"
author: "Student Name"
date: "May 2027"
degree: "Master of Arts in Sociology"     # qc-thesis fills this in
institution: "Queens College"             # one line, or a list of lines
committee:
  - name: "Faculty Member"
    role: "Committee Chair"
  - name: "Second Reader"
    role: "Committee Member"
signatures: true      # signature lines on the title page; qc-thesis default
copyright: true       # adds a copyright page
toc: true
acknowledgements: |
  ...
abstract: |
  ...
output:
  docdesigner::pdf:
    style: qc-thesis
---

Each level-one heading (#) is a chapter. signatures: false removes the signature block. Any style can use the thesis layout with title_layout: thesis under docdesigner::pdf:.

Per-style details — body font, accent colour, section numbering, column count — are not listed here on purpose. A hand-written table of them lived at this spot and silently went stale: after the rebuilt styles were promoted on 2026-08-26, every accent colour in it was wrong. The Style Gallery vignette builds the same table from the installed styles, so it cannot drift:

vignette("style-gallery", package = "docdesigner")
designer_styles()               # id, label, description, set
designer_style("policy")        # the fully resolved token spec

Inspect styles from R:

docdesigner::designer_styles()
docdesigner::designer_style("policy")
docdesigner::designer_gallery()

Use a style:

output:
  docdesigner::pdf:
    style: methods

Creating Styles

A style is a folder with a format.yml file of design tokens. Built-in styles ship inside two sets, academic and public:

inst/sets/
  academic/
    set.yml
    styles/
      minimal/
        format.yml
  public/
    set.yml
    styles/
      policy/
        format.yml

Tokens are written as flat dotted keys — one key: value per line. Only the identity keys (id, label, description) and the tokens that differ from the defaults need to appear:

id: my-style
label: My Style
description: A concise description of where this style should be used

typography.body: "Source Serif 4"
typography.heading: "Source Serif 4"
typography.base_size: "10pt"

color.accent: "005EA8"
color.rule: "005EA8"

headings.number_sections: true
headings.h1.scale: 1.30

title.layout: header
code.highlight: tango

Scaffold a new style from an existing one, then edit only what differs:

docdesigner::designer_new_style("my-style", from = "minimal")

Validate it against the token schema before rendering:

docdesigner::designer_validate_style("my-style")

docdesigner::designer_tokens() lists every available token with its type, allowed values, default, and implementation status. The Creating a style article documents the whole vocabulary. Use a local style by its folder path:

output:
  docdesigner::pdf:
    style: "path/to/my-style"

Keep styles declarative. They describe a visual system through tokens, not arbitrary R code.

Optional YAML

Common fields:

subtitle: "Subtitle"
date: "`r format(Sys.Date(), '%B %d, %Y')`"
abstract: |
  Short abstract.
keywords:
  - keyword one
  - keyword two
bibliography: references.bib
csl: default.csl

Diagnostics

Run:

docdesigner::designer_check()

This checks package assets, style bundles, rmarkdown, Pandoc, and common LaTeX engines.
